about: Explicit adjudications for the audit corpus's intent_invariant and design_adjudication cases (M04 remediation). Each entry names a predicate in test_m04_audit_corpus.py. decision=residual_ambiguity marks a case the deterministic grammar cannot resolve without lexical semantics (design D2); it is reported, never counted as a pass.

M04-C0002.reason: mid-clause punctuation name followed by a word after a transitive verb: surface-identical to the supported command position ('hello comma how are you' LF-SYN-025, 'cat notes dot txt pipe grep today' LF-SYN-035). Deciding that the next word is a compound-noun head needs part-of-speech knowledge a deterministic grammar does not have (design D2); the clause-start, determiner and lexical guards cover the other variants of this family. Escape: 'write the word period'.

M04-C0009.reason: utterance-final 'period' after a noun: surface-identical to the accepted positive 'stop period' → 'stop.' (LF-SYN-026, SC corpus). The curated 'X period' compound list (grace/trial/notice/…) stays, but adding each new noun is the blacklist growth the audit rejects (design D2). Escape: 'write the word period'.

M04-C0295.reason: utterance-initial 'slash <exact registered alias>' is the accepted command form ('slash brainstorm' → '/brainstorm', LF-SYN-015 / SC-01). With 'costs' registered as a skill, 'slash costs' is surface-identical; the repair removes the verb-context readings (REGISTRY-03/-05 now literal) but cannot infer intent here without lexical semantics (design D2).

M04-C0301.reason: the comma is a structural barrier: 'twenty' stays a separate word (no following noun) and 'five percent' may convert on its own side; never 25%

M04-C0302.reason: the sentence period is a structural barrier: two quantities, never 105%; the period itself survives

M04-C0314.reason: count + duration: a clock time needs time evidence (an anchor word or a spoken meridiem) and never precedes a duration unit; juxtaposed number words stay words rather than become ambiguous adjacent digits

M04-C0329.reason: already-written code: text between backtick fences (and inline backticks) is protected existing syntax (layer 2) — nothing inside is normalized

M04-C0332.reason: spoken email components keep the user's spelling: the local part is case-significant, so 'UserName' is never lower-cased; whole literal also acceptable

M04-C0357.reason: narrow calendar check adopted: a day beyond the month's maximum (Feb 29) is flagged invalid_day, never rendered

M04-C0358.reason: narrow calendar check adopted: Feb 29 with an explicit non-leap year is flagged invalid_date, never rendered

M04-C0359.reason: no year spoken: Feb 29 is a possible date; rendered without inventing a year, value 02-29 (not calendar-certified against a year)

M04-C0360.reason: explicit leap year: valid, rendered with the year

M04-C0361.reason: bare year speech without a date is not converted (existing year-speak guard); whole literal

M04-C0364.reason: no arithmetic grammar exists; operands must not be partially digitized ('5 minus three') or re-signed ('-3'): whole literal

M04-C0365.reason: endpoints and the through relation preserved; whole literal is the current outcome

M04-C0367.reason: no anchor and no meridiem: not a clock time, not a code (codes need an anchor), not a count — whole literal

M04-C0368.reason: 'literally' is not a supported escape (only 'write the word(s)/phrase'); 'period' after a word at the end of an utterance is the ordinary command position, so 'literally.' is the declared behaviour — the supported escape remains 'write the word period'
